title: Surrogate Substitution Preserves PHI Detectability: A Multi-Detector Equivalence Study
abstract: arXiv:2608.03172v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Structure-preserving de-identification replaces protected health information (PHI) with realistic same-type surrogates -- "Anna S." becomes "Maria S.", not [NAME] -- so that clinical text stays fluent and downstream tools keep working. But this only helps if the substitution does not itself corrupt the signal those tools rely on. We ask a narrow, testable question: on the spans a de-identifier actually masks, can downstream PHI detectors still find the surrogate? We introduce a paired, multi-detector evaluation protocol that (i) scores utility only on masked spans, decoupling coverage from utility; (ii) uses equivalence testing (TOST) rather than null-hypothesis significance testing, which is uninformative at our sample size (57k paired spans); and (iii) builds a surrogate-failure typology separating fixable generator defects from intrinsic detector limits. translated_title: 替代替换保持PHI可检测性：一项多检测器等价性研究
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.03172v3 公告类型：替换 摘要：结构保留的去标识化将受保护健康信息（PHI）替换为逼真的同类型替代物——“Anna S.”变为“Maria S.”，而非[姓名]——从而保持临床文本流畅，并确保下游工具继续正常工作。但这仅在替换本身不破坏这些工具所依赖的信号时才有帮助。我们提出一个狭窄且可检验的问题：在去标识器实际掩盖的跨度上，下游PHI检测器是否仍能发现替代物？我们引入了一种成对的多检测器评估协议，该协议（i）仅在掩盖的跨度上评分效用，将覆盖范围与效用解耦；（ii）使用等价性检验（TOST）而非零假设显著性检验，后者在我们的样本量（57,000个成对跨度）下无信息量；（iii）构建了一个替代物失败类型学，将可修复的生成器缺陷与固有的检测器限制区分开来。在11个检测器、7个基准和7种语言（1,750篇文档）上，召回率...
tldr: 本文提出了一种成对多检测器评估协议，通过等价性检验和仅在掩盖跨度上评分，验证结构保留的PHI替代物能否被下游检测器可靠识别，并区分生成器缺陷与检测器固有局限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a paired multi-detector evaluation protocol using equivalence testing and masked-span scoring to verify whether structure-preserving PHI surrogates remain detectable by downstream detectors, while distinguishing generator defects from inherent detector limits.
